objective_pt: Entender e usar expressões idiomáticas comuns (piece of cake, under the weather, call it a day) sem traduzir as do português ao pé da letra.

teacher.goal_pt: Mostrar que expressões não se traduzem palavra por palavra e descobrir quais o aluno já conhece.
prompts: Do you know any English idioms?
What's a Brazilian expression that would be hard to translate?
watchFor: Traduzir "custou os olhos da cara" literalmente; em inglês é "cost an arm and a leg".
Usar a expressão no contexto errado só porque conhece as palavras.

exercises.prompt: Don't worry, the test was a piece of cake.
accepted: Don't worry, the test was a piece of cake.
Do not worry, the test was a piece of cake.

exercises.instruction_pt: "It was a piece of cake" means...
exercises.explanation_pt: "A piece of cake" é algo muito fácil, como o nosso "moleza" ou "mamão com açúcar".

exercises.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Esse celular custou os olhos da cara."
accepted: This phone cost an arm and a leg
That phone cost an arm and a leg
This phone cost me an arm and a leg
This phone cost a fortune
This phone cost me a fortune
This phone was really expensive
This phone was super expensive
This phone was extremely expensive
This cell phone cost an arm and a leg

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Os olhos da cara" não funciona em inglês. A expressão equivalente é "cost an arm and a leg" (um braço e uma perna).
commonErrors.correction_en: This phone cost an arm and a leg.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: O passado de "cost" é "cost", sem "-ed".
commonErrors.correction_en: This phone cost an arm and a leg.

teacher.goal_pt: Aprender expressões idiomáticas frequentes no trabalho e no dia a dia.
prompts: When do you feel under the weather?
What's something you do once in a blue moon?
watchFor: Mudar palavras da expressão ("under the time", "in a blue moon"); expressões são fixas.
Usar expressões informais em contexto muito formal.

exercises.example_en: I'm feeling a bit under the weather today, so I'll work from home.

exercises.meaning_pt: encerrar o dia, parar por hoje
exercises.example_en: It's eight o'clock. Let's call it a day.
He told a joke to break the ice at the start of the meeting.

exercises.instruction_pt: Match each idiom to its meaning.

pairs.en: the ball is in your court
hit the nail on the head

exercises.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Ainda estou em cima do muro sobre essa decisão."
accepted: I'm still on the fence about this decision
I'm still on the fence about that decision
I'm still on the fence about the decision
I'm still on the fence about it
I'm still undecided about this decision
I still haven't made up my mind about this decision
I'm still sitting on the fence about this decision
I'm still torn about this decision

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Em cima do muro" em inglês é "on the fence" (na cerca), não "on the wall".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm still on the fence about this decision.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Dizemos "on the fence about" algo.
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm still on the fence about this decision.

teacher.goal_pt: Treinar o ritmo das expressões: palavras de conteúdo fortes e "a", "the", "of" fracos.
prompts: Say "a piece of cake". Which words are strong?
Say "an arm and a leg" as one phrase.
watchFor: Separar as palavras demais, quebrando o ritmo da expressão.

exercises.prompt: That holiday cost us an arm and a leg.
accepted: That holiday cost us an arm and a leg.
That vacation cost us an arm and a leg.

exercises.prompt: We only go out for dinner once in a blue moon.
accepted: We only go out for dinner once in a blue moon.
We only go out to dinner once in a blue moon.

exercises.instruction_pt: In "a piece of cake", which words are stressed?
exercises.explanation_pt: As palavras de conteúdo ("piece", "cake") são fortes; "a" e "of" ficam fracas e rápidas.

teacher.goal_pt: Entender expressões idiomáticas pelo contexto e reagir a elas.
prompts: What does it mean when someone says "I'm swamped"?
How would you answer "Let's call it a day"?
watchFor: Usar a expressão certa com a preposição errada.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. What does the speaker mean?
exercises.listen: I've sent them our offer. Now the ball is in their court.
options: Now it's their turn to decide.
exercises.explanation_pt: "The ball is in their court" quer dizer que agora a decisão é deles.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and answer: why isn't Paula at work today?
exercises.listen: Paula's not coming in today. She's a bit under the weather.
accepted: Because she's sick
She's sick
She's not feeling well
Because she isn't feeling well
Because she's not feeling well
She's feeling a bit ill
She's a little sick
She's feeling sick
Because she's ill
She's ill
She's under the weather
Because she's under the weather
She's not well

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Under the weather" não tem a ver com o tempo: significa estar meio doente.
commonErrors.correction_en: Because she's not feeling well.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Falta o verbo "be": "she's sick" (she is sick).
commonErrors.correction_en: Because she's sick.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. Agree to stop working for today, using an idiom.
exercises.listen: We've been working on this for ten hours. I'm exhausted.
accepted: Let's call it a day
Me too. Let's call it a day
Yeah, let's call it a day
Okay, let's call it a day
I'm exhausted too. Let's call it a day
Why don't we call it a day?
Shall we call it a day?
Let's call it a night
Me too, let's call it a night

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Encerrar o dia" tem uma expressão própria: "Let's call it a day".
commonErrors.correction_en: Let's call it a day.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Depois de "let's" o verbo vem sem "to": "Let's call it a day".
commonErrors.correction_en: Let's call it a day.

teacher.goal_pt: Usar duas ou três expressões naturalmente numa conversa sobre a semana ou o trabalho.
prompts: How was your week? Was it a piece of cake or a nightmare?
Is there a decision you're on the fence about?
What's something that costs an arm and a leg in Brazil?
watchFor: Encaixar expressões à força; elas devem aparecer quando cabem.
Traduzir expressões brasileiras ao pé da letra ("pagar o pato", "chover no molhado").

exercises.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Está chovendo canivete, vamos ficar em casa."
accepted: It's raining cats and dogs, let's stay home
It's raining cats and dogs, let's stay at home
It's raining cats and dogs, so let's stay home
It's raining cats and dogs, so let's stay in
It's pouring, let's stay home
It's pouring down, let's stay home
It's pouring, so let's stay in
It's raining really hard, let's stay home
It's raining heavily, let's stay at home

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Chovendo canivete" em inglês é "raining cats and dogs" ou só "pouring".
commonErrors.correction_en: It's raining cats and dogs, let's stay home.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Ficar em casa" é "stay home", "stay at home" ou "stay in". "In home" não se usa.
commonErrors.correction_en: Let's stay home.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Quem pagou o pato fui eu."
accepted: I was the one who took the blame
I'm the one who took the blame
I was the one who took the fall
I took the blame
I ended up taking the blame
I took the fall
I was the one who got blamed
I got the blame
I was left holding the bag
I was left holding the baby

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Pagar o pato" não existe em inglês. Diga "take the blame" ou "take the fall".
commonErrors.correction_en: I was the one who took the blame.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A ordem "quem... fui eu" fica melhor em inglês como "I was the one who...".
commonErrors.correction_en: I was the one who took the blame.

accepted: You hit the nail on the head with that comment

exercises.instruction_pt: Tell a friend about your week. Use at least two idioms from this unit.
exercises.prompt_en: Hey! Long time no see. How's everything going? How was your week?
guidelines_pt: Describe something easy or hard: "It was a piece of cake" or "I was swamped".
Mention a cost or a decision: "cost an arm and a leg", "I'm on the fence about..."
End naturally: "Anyway, I should call it a day."

teacher.goal_pt: Revisar as expressões e reforçar que elas são fixas.
prompts: What's a piece of cake for you?
What do you do once in a blue moon?

exercises.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Você acertou em cheio."
accepted: You hit the nail on the head
You've hit the nail on the head
You nailed it
You got it exactly right
You're absolutely right
Spot on
You're spot on
That's spot on

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Acertar em cheio" é "hit the nail on the head", "nail it" ou "spot on".
commonErrors.correction_en: You hit the nail on the head.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A preposição é "on": "hit the nail on the head".
commonErrors.correction_en: You hit the nail on the head.

exercises.sentence: He told a funny story to break the ___.
accepted: ice

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A expressão é fixa: "break the ice", como "quebrar o gelo".
commonErrors.correction_en: He told a funny story to break the ice.

exercises.prompt: It's been a long day. I think it's time to call it a day.
accepted: It's been a long day. I think it's time to call it a day.
It has been a long day. I think it is time to call it a day.

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat out loud.
practice.prompt: Sorry, I can't come tonight. I'm a bit under the weather.
accepted: Sorry, I can't come tonight. I'm a bit under the weather.
Sorry, I can't make it tonight. I'm a bit under the weather.

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat out loud.
practice.prompt: We've done enough for today. Let's call it a day.
accepted: We've done enough for today. Let's call it a day.
We've done enough for today. Let's call it a night.

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat out loud.
practice.prompt: The exam was a piece of cake.
accepted: The exam was a piece of cake.
The test was a piece of cake.

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat out loud.
practice.prompt: Telling a joke is a great way to break the ice.
accepted: Telling a joke is a great way to break the ice.
Telling a joke is a good way to break the ice.

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat. Link the words: fingers-crossed.
practice.prompt: I'll keep my fingers crossed for your interview.
accepted: I'll keep my fingers crossed for your interview.
I'm keeping my fingers crossed for your interview.

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat out loud.
practice.prompt: Don't worry, it's not rocket science.
accepted: Don't worry, it's not rocket science.

practice.word_en: to cost an arm and a leg
practice.example_en: That new phone costs an arm and a leg.
I'm exhausted. I'm going to hit the sack.

practice.meaning_pt: estar em cima do muro, indeciso
practice.example_en: I'm still on the fence about buying a car.

practice.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Esse carro custou os olhos da cara."
accepted: That car cost an arm and a leg
This car cost an arm and a leg
That car was really expensive
That car cost a fortune
This car cost a fortune
That car was super expensive

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Não traduza ao pé da letra. A expressão em inglês é "cost an arm and a leg".
commonErrors.correction_en: That car cost an arm and a leg.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Cost" é irregular: o passado é "cost".
commonErrors.correction_en: That car cost an arm and a leg.

practice.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Minha irmã ainda está em cima do muro sobre o casamento."
accepted: My sister is still on the fence about the wedding
My sister's still on the fence about the wedding
My sister is still undecided about the wedding
My sister still hasn't made up her mind about the wedding
My sister is still on the fence about getting married
My sister is still unsure about the wedding

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Em inglês a expressão é "on the fence" (cerca), não "wall".
commonErrors.correction_en: My sister is still on the fence about the wedding.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Use "about": "on the fence about".
commonErrors.correction_en: My sister is still on the fence about the wedding.

practice.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Vou dormir, estou morto de cansaço."
accepted: I'm going to hit the sack, I'm exhausted
I'm going to bed, I'm exhausted
I'm going to hit the sack. I'm dead tired
I'm going to bed. I'm dead tired
I'm off to bed, I'm exhausted
I'm going to hit the sack, I'm worn out
I'm going to bed, I'm worn out

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Morto de cansaço" é "exhausted" ou "dead tired".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm going to bed, I'm exhausted.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Use "I'm going to bed" ou "hit the sack".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm going to bed.

practice.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Foi moleza!"
accepted: It was a piece of cake
It was really easy
It was a breeze
That was a piece of cake
It was super easy
It was easy peasy

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Moleza" não se traduz por "soft". Use "a piece of cake" ou "a breeze".
commonErrors.correction_en: It was a piece of cake.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A expressão é "a piece of cake".
commonErrors.correction_en: It was a piece of cake.

practice.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Ontem a gente encerrou o expediente às cinco."
accepted: Yesterday we called it a day at five
We called it a day at five yesterday
Yesterday we called it a day at five o'clock
Yesterday we finished work at five
We finished work at five yesterday
Yesterday we stopped working at five

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A expressão é "call it a day", com "a".
commonErrors.correction_en: Yesterday we called it a day at five.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Expediente" não se traduz por "expedient". Use "call it a day" ou "finish work".
commonErrors.correction_en: Yesterday we called it a day at five.

practice.instruction_pt: Say it in English: "Vou torcer por você."
accepted: I'll keep my fingers crossed for you
I'm keeping my fingers crossed for you
I'll be rooting for you
I'm rooting for you
Fingers crossed for you
I'll cross my fingers for you

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Torcer" por alguém é "root for" ou "keep your fingers crossed". "Twist" é torcer um objeto.
commonErrors.correction_en: I'll keep my fingers crossed for you.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Use "root for you" ou "cheer you on".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'll be rooting for you.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and say you are not feeling well. Use an idiom.

accepted: I'm feeling a bit under the weather
I'm a bit under the weather
I'm feeling under the weather today

I'm feeling a bit under the weather today
I'm not feeling very well

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A expressão é "under the weather".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm feeling a bit under the weather.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Use "under", não "below": "under the weather".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm a bit under the weather.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and suggest stopping for the day.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Depois de "let's" o verbo vem sem "to".

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and say the task was very easy. Use an idiom.

No, it was a breeze
It was a breeze

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A expressão é "a piece of cake".
commonErrors.correction_en: It was a piece of cake.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Falta o sujeito: "It was a piece of cake".
commonErrors.correction_en: It was a piece of cake.

hay

commonErrors.correction_en: A good game can help break the ice.

accepted: Don't worry it's not rocket science

practice.instruction_pt: Role-play. Chat with a colleague at the end of the day.
practice.scene_pt: It's Friday evening. You and your colleague Mia are still in the office.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Phew, what a week. Are you still working on that presentation?

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Diga que sim, mas que está quase terminando e que foi moleza.
accepted: Yes, but I'm almost done. It was a piece of cake
Yeah, but I'm nearly finished. It was a piece of cake
Yes, but I'm almost finished. It was a breeze
Yes, but I'm almost done. It was really easy
Yeah, almost done. It was a piece of cake

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A expressão é "a piece of cake".
commonErrors.correction_en: It was a piece of cake.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Use "almost done" ou "almost finished".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm almost done.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Lucky you. I'm feeling a bit under the weather, to be honest.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Diga que sente muito e sugira que ela encerre por hoje.
accepted: Oh, I'm sorry. Why don't you call it a day?
Sorry to hear that. You should call it a day
I'm sorry to hear that. Maybe you should call it a day
Oh no. Why don't you call it a day and go home?
Sorry to hear that. Why don't you call it a day?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A expressão é "call it a day".
commonErrors.correction_en: Why don't you call it a day?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: A expressão é "sorry to hear that".
commonErrors.correction_en: Sorry to hear that.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Good idea. By the way, are you going to Jake's leaving party tomorrow?

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Diga que ainda está em cima do muro.
accepted: I'm still on the fence
I'm still on the fence about it
I don't know, I'm still on the fence
I'm not sure yet. I'm on the fence
I haven't made up my mind yet

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Em inglês: "on the fence".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm still on the fence.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Use "on the fence".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm still on the fence.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Oh, come on, you should come! It'll be fun.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Diga que tudo bem, você vai, e que vai torcer para ela melhorar.
accepted: Okay, I'll go. And I'll keep my fingers crossed that you feel better
Fine, I'll come. I hope you feel better soon
Okay, I'll be there. Fingers crossed you feel better
Alright, I'll come. I hope you feel better
Okay, I'll go. Get well soon

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Torcer" é "keep your fingers crossed" ou "hope".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'll keep my fingers crossed that you feel better.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Depois de "hope", o mais natural é o presente: "I hope you feel better".
commonErrors.correction_en: I hope you feel better soon.

practice.instruction_pt: Tell a short story using at least three idioms.
practice.prompt_en: Tell me about a busy or difficult day you had recently. Try to use some idioms.
guidelines_pt: Use idioms like "under the weather", "a piece of cake", "call it a day"
Tell it in order: "First... Then... In the end..."
Don't translate Portuguese idioms word for word.
